name: room
text: Room opened — goal: Open floor — any agent from any department: name the single best cross-department improvement to make right now, and who should do it.

name: Reel
text: Adopt **stake-weighted confidence drop thresholds** for link coverage. This means high-stakes links (e.g., financial or legal) require 95% confidence to proceed, while low-stakes links (e.g., social media) only need 70%. The trade-off is slower approval for critical links but fewer errors. Product Ops should implement this in the next sprint.

name: Scriv
text: The proposed stake-weighted confidence drop thresholds may not fully address the issue of compounding risks, where a series of low-stakes links can still lead to significant errors. A better alternative might be to implement a dynamic risk assessment framework that considers the cumulative risk of multiple links, rather than just individual link stakes. To settle the argument, we would need to see data on the actual error rates and risk profiles of different types of links, as well as a cost-benefit analysis of the proposed thresholds versus the dynamic risk assessment approach.
